page: Vultr vcg-a16-12c-128g-32vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz. The processor features a cache layout of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3, supporting AVX, AES, and FMA instructions. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. For hardware acceleration, it integrates two NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 700 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in machine learning and data processing. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds of 8665.1 tokens per second and a strong text generation rate of 260.3 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 613.27 tokens per second with text generation at 32.35 tokens per second. General compute benchmarks show a stress-ng single-core score of 1754.67 and a multi-core score of 21080.54. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only small block speeds of 1191.06 GB/sec and large block write speeds of 53.61 GB/sec.

This hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for GPU-accelerated workloads, combining dual NVIDIA A16 GPUs with a substantial 128.0 GB memory footprint. The shared CPU allocation represents a cost-efficient tradeoff for workloads that are primarily GPU-bound rather than CPU-bound. This server is optimized for workloads such as low-to-medium parameter LLM inference, graphics rendering, video transcoding, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.

This configuration represents a resource-dense, cost-efficient option for GPU-accelerated tasks where shared CPU allocation is acceptable. It is highly suited for small-to-medium LLM inference, media streaming, and parallel data processing workloads.
